Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a production editable-face game sprite sheet, one unified raster asset. The attached portrait is a STYLE reference only: preserve its handsome natural ink-and-paint illustration quality, warm cel shading, crisp but human features and gentle eyes. Do not make a procedural avatar or caricature.
Create EXACTLY SIXTEEN DIFFERENT FICTIONAL ADULT people, a strict 4 by 4 grid of equally sized SQUARE complete head-and-shoulder portraits, ideally 2048x2048. NO gutters, labels, words or numbers. All cells have the same flat taupe background, same lighting, scale, frontal pose and purple/cream V-neck basketball jersey. EVERY person must be COMPLETELY BALD and CLEAN SHAVEN, to accept separate hair and beard layers. Natural attractive shaved scalp, not sickly or uncanny. No lashes exaggerated, no jewelry, glasses, beard, hair, mustache or headband.
REGISTRATION CRITICAL: in EVERY square, head center x50%; bare skull top y14%; skull temples x30% and70% at y33%; eyes centered at x41%/59%, y40%; nose tip at50%,y50%; mouth center50%,y60%; chin50%,y72%; ears around x28%/72%,y47%; neck to y85%; jersey begins at y83%. No head tilt. Keep eyelids calm, pupils centered, lips naturally closed. Differing face widths, cheeks, eye shape, noses and lips are subtle natural identity differences around these shared anchors; all share a compatible scalp outline for hair layers. Show varied rounded, oval, broad, softer and angular faces; do not give everyone the same sharp jaw.
Read left to right, top to bottom: 1 East Asian man light-medium warm skin, narrow oval face; 2 Black man deep brown skin, broad balanced face; 3 European man fair skin, softer rectangular face; 4 South Asian man medium brown skin, oval face; 5 West Asian man olive skin, prominent but natural nose; 6 mixed Black/East Asian man warm brown skin, rounded cheeks; 7 Indigenous American man medium bronze skin, broad cheekbones; 8 Pacific Islander man tan-brown skin, broad softer face; 9 Black man very deep skin, long oval face; 10 European man fair freckled skin, narrower face; 11 mixed European/East Asian man light tan skin, rounder features; 12 Latin American man medium tan skin with distinct rounded nose; 13 East Asian woman light-medium skin, softly oval mature adult face; 14 Black woman deep brown skin, broad cheeks; 15 European woman fair skin, mature softly angular face; 16 mixed South Asian/European woman medium warm skin, rounded mature adult face. All are adults 25-45, diverse humans rather than racial caricatures.
Keep the polished illustrated style EXACTLY consistent across all sixteen and with the reference. Opaque finished portraits. No scary faces, photorealism, glossy 3D, oversized eyes, giant eyebrows or heavy dark rings around eyes. Facial highlights and shadows must look like the reference illustration.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: ONE transparent painted hairstyle SPRITE SHEET for the face editor. Input 1 is the exact placement guide: a bald head whose scalp starts at y22% of its square, temples x30%/70% at y39%, eyebrows y43%, eyes y47%, ears around y53%, chin y78%. Input 2 defines the beautiful refined ink/cel-painted hair style. Create ONLY THE HAIR that fits over Input 1. DO NOT DRAW the head, face, forehead, scalp skin, eyebrows, ears, neck, jersey, background or mannequin. Those areas must be truly transparent. All sixteen cells use identical skull placement, pose, scale, forehead edge and illumination; only hairstyles change. Natural black/soft-black hair with warm dark-brown highlights, hand-inked strand detail, not a flat vector silhouette and not photographic.
Output EXACTLY 4 columns by 4 rows of equally sized SQUARE cells, ideally 2048x2048. No gutters, grid lines, labels, text or cast shadow outside the hair. Fully transparent background/negative space. Each is a complete hair overlay in its cell, no parts crossing cell boundaries. Keep all hair comfortably inside cell (top y3% or lower, sides x5%-95%). Common hairline is near y35%-38% in the center; no fringe touches the eyes. Match the scalp contour from the guide; the hair wraps snugly around the skull rather than floating above it.
Order left to right, top to bottom:
1 Swept side part; 2 Short textured crop with tapered sides; 3 Very short buzz cut, soft semi-transparent scalp stubble and solid fine hairline, NO skin; 4 Crew cut with short upright 2-3cm top and tapered sides.
5 Mid fade, textured short crown, faded translucent short side hairs; 6 Caesar cut, short straight horizontal fringe; 7 Close-cut 360 waves, inked wave arcs, no skin; 8 Short natural afro, tight small coily curls close to skull.
9 Large rounded afro, textured tightly coiled volume, full shape; 10 Short individual two-strand twists with tapered sides; 11 Frohawk, coily upright strip with faded sides; 12 Narrow upright mohawk, straight/wavy spikes, shaved sides transparent.
13 Short individual locs around head, above ears; 14 Long individual locs draping along BOTH sides of the invisible face and ending at shoulders y94%, no locs over eyes or center face; 15 Locs pulled up into a high tied knot with short sides; 16 Neat tight cornrows from natural hairline backward, scalp gaps transparent.
Critical: this is a transparent HAIR LAYER asset, not sixteen portraits. Leave every face/skin/jersey pixel transparent. Preserve the reference illustration's gentle natural drawing quality. No creepy face appears anywhere because no face is included.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: ONE transparent facial-hair layer sheet for an illustrated basketball face editor. The first input is the exact bald face geometry: mouth centered at x50%,y65%, nose tip y57%, chin x50%,y78%, jaw corners x35%/65% at y70%, sideburns x31%/69% from y52%. The second input is the approved inked painted art style.
Create 16 equally sized SQUARE cells in a strict 4 by 4 grid, ideally 2048x2048. EVERY cell shares that same geometry and placement. Leave the TOP HALF of every cell completely transparent. Draw ONLY facial hair that fits onto the guide's face. NO skin, lips, mouth, nose, ears, head, hair on scalp, neck, jersey, background, numbers, labels, frames or shadows. Leave the shape of the lips transparent and keep all beard hair below the nose. Paint believable fine soft-black/dark-brown strands with the reference's refined ink/cel illustration, natural beard contours, not pasted solid black stamps. All facial hair fits inside its square, no neighbouring cells.
Order left to right, top to bottom:
1 Stubble: delicate sparse short hairs over cheeks, jaw, mustache and chin, with real transparency between hairs. 2 Heavy stubble, denser close-cropped short hairs. 3 Patchy beard, naturally uneven separated small areas on jaw and chin. 4 Mustache ONLY, neat natural shape under the nose, no beard.
5 Soul patch ONLY, tiny tuft directly below lower lip. 6 Chin puff ONLY, soft small patch on chin. 7 Goatee ONLY, trimmed chin beard and small mustache not connected at sides of mouth. 8 Circle beard, connected mustache and neatly trimmed goatee around transparent lips.
9 Van Dyke, pointed small chin beard and separate tidy mustache, clean cheeks. 10 Chinstrap, narrow connected hair along jaw from sideburns to chin, no mustache. 11 Chinstrap plus mustache. 12 Short beard, neat fuller beard following jaw and cheeks, transparent mouth/lips.
13 Full beard, natural fuller medium beard with distinct strand detail, ends no lower than y87%. 14 Thick beard, dense fuller beard with natural soft contour, ends no lower than y90%, not huge or comic. 15 Thin pencil mustache. 16 Long goatee, longer pointed chin hair ending at y88%, mustache separate.
CRITICAL: black/soft-black beard hair only with genuine alpha. No portrait is drawn, only the facial hair overlays; the face beneath must remain fully visible and unaltered. No broad opaque gray shadow where clean-shaven skin should show. No creepy face or fake checkerboard.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: one TRANSPARENT clothing layer sheet for the same illustrated face editor. Input 1 is the bald head/neck/jersey placement guide. Input 2 supplies the painted grey staff clothing style. Produce FOUR square clothing overlays in a strict 2 by 2 grid, ideally 1536x1536. Every cell has an identical front-facing shoulder/neck pose and scale. Draw ONLY the CLOTHES in the lower quarter of the cell; leave the top 74% entirely transparent. Never draw the head, face, hair, skin, neck, background, hands, labels, grid lines or words. Neck opening remains truly transparent. In every square the invisible neck is centered at x50%, width x40%-60%; shoulders spread to edges at bottom. Collar starts at y80%-84%, clothes extend to the bottom edge, no gap below. Follow guide's same garment footprint but replace its jersey as described. Use the reference's refined warm ink/cel-painted shading and natural cloth folds, not photographic fabric or flat vector shapes.
Top left: dark charcoal collared polo shirt, short open placket, like a basketball assistant coach. Top right: grey suit jacket with lapels over a dark charcoal open-collar shirt, no tie. Bottom left: a tailored charcoal collared blouse / staff shirt, restrained natural shape. Bottom right: grey suit jacket with cream shirt and a narrow dark tie. The four are clothing layers only, no people or skin anywhere. Fill the bottom corners with cloth so no basketball jersey peeks out below. Upper head/face region is completely transparent. No random detached pixels.
